system_boundary: In-scope is the two-tank filling/transfer/drain batch system including TK-101, TK-102, XV-101/102/103, LT-101/102, SRC-101, DRN-101, and PLC-101 with its operator pushbuttons and command logic. External to the model are the physical liquid supply/drain boundaries and the operator as a disturbance/input source; the model responds to these boundaries but does not create them.

open_questions.question: Should the ambiguous duplicate requirement set for XV-101 high-level trigger use 0.78 m or 0.80 m as the canonical threshold in the model, or should both be modeled as separate conflicting constraints/notes?
candidates: Model both as conflicting source requirements

open_questions.question: The shutdown sequence requirements conflict/overlap on whether V2 and V3 are allowed to be simultaneously open only during SHUTDOWN. Should the model treat this as an explicit SHUTDOWN exception to the normal interlock?
candidates: Yes, treat SHUTDOWN as an exception allowing V2 and V3 open together
No, keep the interlock always active and flag the conflict

open_questions.question: The contract contains multiple timing values for post-transfer and inter-cycle waits (10 s, 12 s, 8 s) across different requirement sets. Which should be used for the final model defaults?
candidates: 10 s wait after T1 high/low/T2 low
12 s post-transfer delay and 8 s inter-cycle delay
Keep all as separate conflicting requirement variants

open_questions.question: The contract includes both generic controller/tank entities and a more specific PLC-101 / LT-101 / LT-102 / XV-101..103 set. Should the model include both sets as alternative examples, or only the explicitly operational PLC-101-based implementation?
candidates: Include both generic and specific sets as separate packages
Model generic as abstract and PLC-101 as concrete specialization
